title: Aṅguttara-Nikāya (Pali Text)
shelf_note: PTS Pali text of the Aṅguttara-Nikāya; belongs on a Pali shelf. The 'americana' collection tag is an Internet Archive collection label, not a subject.
structure_note: Catalogue identity is wrong (I7). The record says 'Aṅguttara-Nikāya (Pali Text)', 'Richard Morris & Edmund Hardy (eds.)', 1885 (the date of Part I), but every sampled page is Part V (Hardy, 1900): the preface opens 'In issuing this last volume of the Aṅguttara-Nikāya' and says Hardy finished 'the eleventh Nipāta' in 1898; running heads are 'LXXXVII.13—18 Thera-Vagga. 167', 'CXV.3—4' p. 226, 'XIX.1—XX.1' p. 354 (Dasaka and Ekādasaka Nipātas). It appears to be a second scan of the same volume as 69b99e856ed9e0490990a0b5 ('Aṅguttara-Nikāya, Part V', 1900), whose pages show the same Part V chapters (Ānisaṃsa-vagga, Ekādasaka IX–X). The 3 printed backsteps and 3 repeats are probably front-matter roman numerals or misread numerals; not checked.

book_verdict: The pages are good transcriptions of the PTS edition with a usable English, but the record is mis-catalogued: it is Part V (Hardy, 1900) under a generic title and the 1885 date, and appears to duplicate the separate Part V record. The English pane shows recurring <unclear> and <meta> markup.
reader_summary: This is the last volume (Part V, Books of Tens and Elevens) of the Pali Text Society edition of the Aṅguttara-Nikāya, although the catalogue presents it as the whole work dated 1885. The transcription is of the right text and close to the print, with small diacritic slips. The English is readable and mostly faithful, but it drops or renumbers the variant notes and puts spurious <unclear> tags around clear passages.

title: Aṅguttara-Nikāya, Part V (Pali Text)
shelf_note: PTS Pali text, Aṅguttara-Nikāya Part V (Dasaka and Ekādasaka Nipātas). The collection tags (digitallibraryindia, JaiGyan) are IA source labels.
structure_note: There are 444 page records but pages_count is 439, so five records are not counted by the field. This is the same volume as 69b99e681f30176bf4d3798a (mis-titled 'Aṅguttara-Nikāya (Pali Text)', 1885), whose pages show the same Part V chapters; one of the two is a duplicate record. No backsteps.

book_verdict: A sound transcription of PTS Aṅguttara Part V with small name misreadings. The English is fluent, but on two of four pages it either reassigns a speaker or adds words from the following page. The book duplicates another record of the same volume.
reader_summary: This is the Pali Text Society edition of the Aṅguttara-Nikāya, Part V (Books of Tens and Elevens), and the transcription is of the right text, close to the print apart from a few misread names and dropped footnote markers. The English is readable but not reliable line by line: it sometimes completes a sentence from the next page, adds a speaker who is not on the page, or shifts who asks a question. A reader should check it against the Pali.

title: Atthasālinī (Buddhaghosa's commentary on the Dhammasaṅgaṇī) — PTS Pali
shelf_note: PTS edition (E. Müller, 1897) of Buddhaghosa's Abhidhamma commentary; belongs on the Pali shelf.
structure_note: 5 printed backsteps and 5 repeats. The running head carries two numbers (paragraph and page, e.g. 'Atthasālinī 279. 103'), so some backsteps are probably the paragraph number read as the page number, not scan defects. Not checked further.

ocr_errors.problem: 'sasa' (hare) dropped: the physician prescribes fresh hare's flesh, which is what makes the story work

tr_errors.english: fresh meat was required
tr_errors.problem: following the OCR, the hare is lost, and with it the link between the prescription and the captured hare

tr_errors.english: a venerable teacher who is worthy of cultivation
tr_errors.problem: awkward literalism

ocr_errors.problem: footnote tagged as a signature mark; its marker in the text dropped

tr_errors.english: ...the base should be understood.
tr_errors.problem: the senses listed at the head of the page (place of origin, cause) are dropped

tr_errors.english: in expressions like 'gold-base' or 'jewel-base,' it is an aspect
tr_errors.problem: ākara here means a mine (gold-mine, jewel-mine); 'aspect' gives the wrong sense

tr_errors.source: Rāsaṭṭhena hi viññāṇakkhandhassa ekadeso ekaṃ viññāṇaṃ
tr_errors.english: For one part of the consciousness-aggregate, one single consciousness, is a heap in the sense of a mass.
tr_errors.problem: the argument is garbled: it says that one consciousness is a part of the aggregate taken as a heap

ocr_errors.problem: sayaṃ (oneself) read as sāyaṃ (evening); the English correctly follows the image

tr_errors.english: an Elder nun
tr_errors.problem: 'khīṇāsava' (one whose taints are destroyed, an arahant) dropped

tr_errors.source: Sace gilāno vā avassiko vā atthi
tr_errors.english: If there is a sick person or one who is on a temporary stay
tr_errors.problem: avassika = a monk without a rains retreat (newly ordained), not a temporary visitor

tr_errors.source: Sāyaṃ pana navakatarehi attano upaṭṭhānaṃ anāgatehi yeva
tr_errors.english: As for the afternoon, if those who are junior have not come to attend to him
tr_errors.problem: 'before the juniors come to attend on oneself' becomes a condition

tr_errors.english: Sineru, 28
tr_errors.problem: spelling note dropped

other.note: An index of proper names is 'translated' by inserting <gloss> tags into the entries, even inside parentheses ('Saṃyutta(-nikāya <gloss>collection</gloss>)'). The glosses add clutter and generic words ('division', 'discourse') rather than anything a reader needs

book_verdict: A faithful transcription of the PTS Atthasālinī with small slips. The English works for the stories but loses technical sense in the Abhidhamma exegesis. The typewriter-set index suggests a later reprint whose rights should be checked.
reader_summary: This is the Pali Text Society edition of the Atthasālinī, Buddhaghosa's commentary on the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, and the transcription is of the right text with minor slips (one drops the hare from 'fresh hare's flesh'). The English follows the narrative passages well but blurs technical terms in the exegesis, translating 'mine' as 'aspect' and dropping 'arahant'. The index appears to come from a later reprint.

title: Kathāvatthu (Pali Text)
shelf_note: Arnold C. Taylor's PTS edition of the Kathāvatthu (1894–97), the Abhidhamma book of points of controversy.
structure_note: One printed repeat in 676 pages. The two-volume edition is scanned as one, so the repeat is probably where the second volume begins, or a misread numeral. Nothing else stands out.

tr_errors.english: liberated through right knowledge
tr_errors.problem: the opening word (the tail of 'parikkhīṇabhavasaññojano', whose fetters of becoming are destroyed) is dropped

tr_errors.english: untemporary-liberated
tr_errors.problem: an awkward coinage, but consistent and recoverable

tr_errors.english: a person who has practiced for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship
tr_errors.problem: paṭipanno = one who is practising (on the path), not one who has finished; the tense matters to the argument

tr_errors.english: the sensual desire that accompanies it and the ill will that accompanies it
tr_errors.problem: anusahagata = residual, subtle; 'that accompanies it' changes the sense

tr_errors.english: Does a person … not transcend the fruit of the Stream-Enterer? Yes.
tr_errors.problem: nanu ('has he not…?') is rendered as a negative question, so the 'Yes' reads ambiguously

ocr_errors.image: S a m p a y u t t a k a t h ā . (spaced, centred)

ocr_errors.problem: footnote tagged as a marginal note

tr_errors.english: Just as oil is permeated and entered into sesame seeds
tr_errors.problem: syntax garbled (the oil permeates the sesame)

other.note: '->The Discourse on Associated Phenomena.<-': arrow markup is shown in the reader text, and the end-title of VII.2 is presented as a heading for what follows

book_verdict: A clean transcription of Taylor's PTS Kathāvatthu, with an English that faithfully follows the question-and-answer form. There are a few imprecise technical renderings and one leak of arrow markup.
reader_summary: This is the Pali Text Society edition of the Kathāvatthu, and the transcription is of the right text and very close to the print. The English keeps the debate's question-and-answer form and can be followed, though a few technical words are loose ('has practiced' for one still on the path, 'accompanying' for residual defilements).
